messages.author: b0ce139c6b85e1ef
messages.subject: Skew-t likelihood
parts:
Dear INLA team,

I would like to know if is possible to define in R-inla a skew-t likelihood.
As the package has already implemented the skew-normal likelihood and skew-t is a scale mixture of skew-normal, I thought it would be possible to define it.

I deeply appreciate any feedback.

Sincerely,

Carlos

messages.author: fb2efbf28a86c396
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Skew-t likelihood
parts:
Dear INLA team,

I am also interested in the implementation of a skew-t likelihood in INLA. I have noticed it's recent use in HIV clinical trial settings (via a fully Bayesian implementation) where it was shown to outperform existing methods.

Here is a link to the paper by Sahu et.al deriving the skew-t likelihood:
http://www.southampton.ac.uk/~sks/research/papers/sahudeybranco.pdf

Best,
Joe

messages.author: fb2efbf28a86c396
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Skew-t likelihood
parts:
Thanks again for the speedy reply!

Whilst the skew-normal is definitely a useful first step for my applications, I am currently trying to reproduce results found in the literature that found a skew-t likelihood to be necessary over the skew-normal. The need for heavier-tails was found through a small posterior mean for the df term. 

Cheers,
Joe

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Skew-t likelihood
parts:
Hi,

the issue with the student-t is that its not log concave, and for low
df then this could be an issue (and then complaints will appear to
help@...). I would rather add something with tails no heavier than the
exponential... l

H
